issues.description: The solution implementation declares lecture attributes using snake_case names (e.g. lecture_name, number_of_inscribed_students) but the constructor and all methods use camelCase names (e.g. lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents). This name mismatch means the solution code is inconsistent with the UML/description (which uses camelCase) and will not compile as written, causing confusion for students about the correct attribute names to implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Make attribute names consistent with the UML and the rest of the code. Rename the fields in the solution to camelCase: lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents, numberOfGuestStudents, numberOfLecturers, numberOfTutors (or alternatively change constructor and methods to use the snake_case field names consistently). Ensure all getters, setters, constructor assignments, and toString use the same attribute identifiers so the code compiles and matches the specification.

issues.description: The solution implementation declares the Lecture attributes using snake_case names (e.g. lecture_name, number_of_inscribed_students) while the problem statement UML and the rest of the solution code (constructor and getters/setters) use camelCase identifiers (lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents, etc.). Rename the private fields to: lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents, numberOfGuestStudents, numberOfLecturers, numberOfTutors (or consistently change all usages to the chosen naming style). Prefer camelCase to align with Java conventions and the problem statement.
